title: Braised Short Ribs
subtitle: Beef short ribs slow-braised in red wine until fall-off-the-bone
excerpt: Bone-in short ribs seared hard and then braised in red wine and stock for 3 to 4 hours until the meat falls from the bone and the sauce has reduced to a glossy, deeply flavoured gravy.

recipe.sourceNotes: Short ribs (also called Jacob's ladder or beef finger ribs in British cuts) come from the short section of ribs, with a thick cap of meat and generous marbling. They have become popular in restaurant and home cooking from the 2000s onwards, partly through the influence of American steakhouse culture and partly because the long braise is a forgiving technique: once the meat reaches temperature, a further hour only improves the result. The cut is collagen-rich; the long braise converts this to gelatin, which gives the sauce its glossy, coating quality.

recipeTools.notes: Must be large enough to hold the ribs in a single layer with the lid on.

content.text: Short ribs need time. Three hours minimum; four is better. The meat should pull away from the bone without any resistance and the collagen in the meat should have completely dissolved into the sauce. If it is not there yet, cover and return to the oven. Pat the ribs very dry before searing: wet meat will steam and never develop the deep brown crust that is the flavour base for the whole dish.

Pat the ribs very dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a large casserole over the highest heat. Sear the ribs in batches, 2 to 3 minutes per side, until deeply browned on all faces. Remove and set aside.

Heat the oven to 160 C / fan 140 C / gas 3. Reduce the heat under the casserole to medium. Cook the onion, carrot, and celery for 8 minutes. Add the garlic and tomato puree and stir for 2 minutes. Pour in the wine and scrape up any browned bits. Let it bubble for 2 minutes. Add the stock and herbs.

Return the short ribs to the pot, bone-side down. The liquid should come about halfway up the ribs. Cover tightly and cook in the oven for 3.5 to 4 hours, turning the ribs once halfway through, until the meat is completely tender and pulling from the bone.

Remove the ribs and keep warm. Strain the braising liquid through a fine sieve into a saucepan. Skim the fat, then simmer for 10 to 15 minutes until reduced and glossy. Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve the ribs with creamy mashed potato and the reduced sauce.
